title: fix(plugin-auth)!: a password reset disables the OAuth applications the account registered and revokes the SCIM credentials it minted

_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D1WDVL9JpCQhTUF97fpymtZ)_

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：账号重置密码后（自助找回、管理员强制重置、运维命令行重置），该账号自己注册的 OAuth 应用会被停用，它签发的 SCIM 同步凭据会被吊销；自助重置后，账号还会收到一封邮件，列出停用和吊销了什么，以及保留下来的单点登录与双重验证。
- 为什么做：属于“重置密码结束账号此前的访问方式”这一系列，替账号所有者和平台管理员把重置后仍留着的两类入口一并收口。
- 出错会怎样：被误停用的应用，平台管理员可以在后台重新启用；被吊销的 SCIM 凭据不能恢复，需要管理员重新签发，期间该连接的同步暂停；整个改动可以直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

The rule: a completed password reset disables the OAuth applications the account registered and revokes the SCIM credentials it minted. It keeps the account's single sign-on providers and second factor, and names them to the owner.

- **Which resets.** All four that end the account's other access already: the emailed link and the texted code (self-service), the administrator's `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-password` with `revokeSessionsAndKeys` on (the default), and the operator's `os user set-password`. The code gives no reason to treat the last two differently: both already end the same rows as a self-service reset through `forced-reset-revocation.ts`, so they share the one arm, `endWhatTheAccountRegistered` (`password-reset-ends-added-access.ts`). A routine forced reset (`revokeSessionsAndKeys: false`) ends nothing, as before. A password change disables and revokes nothing.
- **Disable, not delete.** Each OAuth application whose `user_id` is the account and whose `disabled` flag is false or unset is written `disabled: true` (with the whole-second `updated_at` the Disable action writes beside it). The provider then issues it no token, client-credentials tokens included (`invalid_client`), answers its earlier tokens inactive at introspection, and the MCP door refuses every token it holds, whoever authorized it (`mcpConsentAdmits` reads `client.disabled`). A platform administrator can enable it again; its owner cannot. An application another account registered is not read.
- **Revoke, only the account's own.** Each SCIM credential whose minting `user_id` is the account and that is still active is revoked through `revokeScimConnectionCredential`, the administrator's own revoke. A credential another administrator minted, for the same connection or another, is not read.
- **Kept and named.** Single sign-on providers the account registered and its two-factor enrolment are not touched. After a completed self-service reset the account is mailed a new built-in template, `auth.password_reset_notice` (en-US, zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES), on the existing mailer path: how many API keys, linked sign-in accounts and authorized apps the reset ended, each application it disabled and each credential it revoked by name, and the single sign-on providers and second factor it kept. Best-effort, like the change reminder. The forced resets send no notice: each answers its requester with the counts, and the operator's command runs with no mail service.
- **Counts.** Additive: `data.revoked.ownedApps` / `data.revoked.scimCredentials` on the forced reset's response, `revokedOwnedApps` / `revokedScimCredentials` on its ledger row, `ownedAppsDisabled` / `scimCredentialsRevoked` on `setOperatorPassword`'s outcome (printed by `os user set-password`). A disable or revoke that does not land answers the self-service requester an error (5xx, as the other arms do) and counts in the forced reset's `failed`, keeping `complete` false. The credentials are still revoked when an application could not be disabled; the first failure is thrown after both have run.
- **Stores that are not there.** Read and written through the data engine by the rows' own `user_id`, whether or not their plugin is mounted now; an object the deployment does not hold, or a table never created, holds none (`isObjectAbsentError(error, object)` with the object read).
- **The change reminder** (`auth.password_changed_notice`) also lists the applications the account registered that are still enabled and the credentials it minted that are still active, and is sent when the account holds only those.
- Docs: `permissions/authentication.mdx` (what a reset ends, the change reminder, Set / Reset a Password and its response shape, SCIM Connection Credentials), `ai/connect-mcp.mdx` (disabling a client), `deployment/cli.mdx`, `deployment/self-hosting.mdx`, `kernel/runtime-services/email-service.mdx` (ten platform-requested auth mails). The tenant-audit census for plugin-auth is regenerated (one write call site added).

## Tests

Measured first: the new describe in `password-reset-ends-added-access.test.ts` (real `AuthManager` over a real ObjectQL on better-sqlite3, behind the plugin's real route mount) run against this branch's tests with plugin-auth's source restored to the base (`cf2e321bf7d`): **9 failed | 1 passed** (the passing one is the control, a reset that does not complete). Then on the fix: **10 passed**.

<details><summary>Red on the base, then green</summary>

```
base src:  Tests  9 failed | 1 passed | 22 skipped (32)   VERDICT command-exit 1
  the emailed reset … expected { app_desk: false, …(3) } to deeply equal { app_desk: true, …(3) }
  the MCP door … and is refused after it, though its holder reset nothing: expected true to be false
  client-credentials … the grant is refused after it: expected 200 to be greater than or equal to 400
  a password change … expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0
  forced reset … expected { sessions: 1, apiKeys: +0, …(4) } to match object { ownedApps: 2, …(3) }
  operator … expected { outcome: 'set', …(6) } to match object { outcome: 'set', …(3) }
  fail closed … the requester is told: expected 200 to be greater than or equal to 500
  absent stores … TypeError: endWhatTheAccountRegistered is not a function
fix:       Tests  10 passed | 22 skipped (32)               VERDICT command-exit 0
```
</details>

Pinned through the real routes, with controls: the emailed and the texted reset disable both enabled apps the account registered (an already-disabled one is left and not listed) and revoke its credential; the administrator's app and the administrator's credential for the same connection are untouched; the account's `sys_sso_provider` row, `sys_two_factor` row and `two_factor_enabled` are byte-for-byte unchanged; the notice names the apps, the credential, the provider and the second factor. The MCP door admits the administrator's token of the account's app before the reset and refuses it after, while the administrator's own app still admits. A client-credentials app the account registered mints a token before the reset and is refused `invalid_client` after, and its earlier token no longer introspects active. A change keeps apps and credentials and its reminder lists them. The forced reset reports the counts on the response and the ledger row, and with revocation off disables nothing; the operator's outcome carries them. A failing app write answers the self-service requester 5xx (credential still revoked) and leaves the forced reset `failed: 1, complete: false`. A bare engine holding neither object answers none.

## Acceptance notes

- The admin forced reset and `os user set-password` apply the same rule as a self-service reset; only the self-service reset mails the account. Mailing after the administrator's forced reset too is a one-line change if wanted.
- A disabled application keeps its grants and refresh tokens, as the Disable action does; enabling it again serves them again. The owner's own grants were already ended by the reset.
- A revoked SCIM credential stays revoked; the connection's provisioning waits for a newly minted credential, unless another administrator's credential for it is still active.
- The forced reset counts a failure of this arm as one entry in `failed`, whichever of the apps or the credentials failed.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:
1. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/password-reset-ends-added-access.ts` — `endWhatTheAccountRegistered` (the owner-scoped reads, the disable write, the revoke, the failure order).
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/forced-reset-revocation.ts` — `endRegistrations` (the store adapter, `failed` / `complete`).
3. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts` — the notice after the self-service reset.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/password-reset-ends-added-access.test.ts -t 'every reset disables'` — expect `Tests  10 passed | 22 skipped (32)`.
